raw: 27.2 The Lubyanka Files: 29 KGB Training Manuals, 1965–1989[^122]
teaching_note: The inherited count and date span are collection-level claims requiring a dated item inventory, not facts proved by a project landing page. For each item distinguish original title/date/issuer, scan, acquisition and release status, translator/editor, translation date, missing pages and corroboration. The Free Russia Foundation project has a stated interpretive purpose; its announcement, news coverage and downstream summaries are not independent witnesses to every manual [@ageint122].
title: The Lubyanka Files: attributed collection scope and provenance

title: Working with Agents: historical translated-edition provenance

title: Working with Information in Intelligence (1970s)

raw: 27.2.3 Psychological Methods and Manipulation of Agents (1988)[^21]
teaching_note: Treat the inherited title and date as an item-identification claim pending the original scan and translation metadata; the news article is not the manual itself. Analyze the institution's claims about people critically, including coercion and asymmetry, without treating rhetoric as psychological diagnosis or teaching manipulation. A manual's assertion of effectiveness is not an empirical finding [@ageint021].
title: Psychological Methods and Manipulation of Agents (1988): historical critique

raw: 27.2.4 Some Aspects of Training Agents Psychologically (1985)[^21]
teaching_note: Distinguish a historical prescription about training from evidence of what occurred and from evidence of harm or benefit. A secondary news description cannot authenticate the exact edition or validate its psychological categories; do not use them to classify learners, sources or contemporary populations. Human-source protection includes freedom from coercion, not merely secrecy [@ageint021].
title: Some Aspects of Training Agents Psychologically (1985): source and harm limits

raw: 27.2.5 Exposure of Disinformation in Intelligence Materials (1968)[^21]
teaching_note: Completed offline translation case: T1 is a synthetic 1968 catalog entry, T2 a 2019 translated excerpt rendering a term as 'confirmed', T3 a news article repeating T2, and T4 a translator's note proposing 'reported' instead. The filled chain has one textual origin with two interpretations, not three corroborating accounts; the original date, translation date and public-release date occupy different chronology fields. Withheld T5 supplies the surrounding sentence and supports 'reported', so downgrade the content from established fact to an institutional report and annotate the translation correction. Retain the catalog identity but stop any inference that the manual proves actual conduct or present-day continuity (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]).
title: Exposure of Disinformation in Intelligence Materials (1968)

raw: 27.2.6 Organizational Structure and Management of Intelligence Residency
teaching_note: A residency is a historically situated overseas organizational unit, not a software runtime or a template for clandestine organization. The cited analytic standards cannot supply its personnel, reporting lines or management history. Keep those cells unknown unless dated institutional records establish them; no current staff identification or operational reconstruction is required.
title: Historical intelligence residency: structure and source gaps

raw: 27.2.7 On Organizing Work with Confidential Contacts[^122]
teaching_note: A historical term such as 'confidential contact' may denote an institutional category rather than an individual's consent, motive or legal status. Establish its meaning from the relevant dated text and translation, not from a project title or present assumptions. Discuss classification uncertainty and coercion critically without contact-development or elicitation instructions [@ageint122].
title: On Organizing Work with Confidential Contacts: historical terminology

raw: 27.2.8 Tasks of a KGB Resident Abroad[^122]
teaching_note: A resident's prescribed duties are evidence of intended institutional responsibilities, not proof that a person performed them or that current successors do so. Project metadata is a lead to the document, not a substitute for the text. Keep the exercise at the level of dated role descriptions and evidence limitations, with no tasking or emulation [@ageint122].
title: Tasks of a KGB Resident Abroad: intended role versus conduct

raw: 27.6 The Interpreter Magazine: KGB Manual Summaries[^22]
teaching_note: A summary and a translation-project announcement can explain discovery and editorial choices but omit qualifications, pages or terminology needed for substantive historical claims. Compare source families before counting confirmation: a news story, blog and summary drawing on one project remain dependent. Archival survival and publication selection constrain what can be concluded about Soviet practice and provide no automatic evidence of present Russian behavior [@ageint022].
